stem: Rey works in a city procurement office. His supervisor reminds him of Section 7(a) of RA 6713: public officials and employees shall not, directly or indirectly, have any financial or material interest in ___. What completes the rule?
choices: any transaction requiring the approval of their office
any private business, even one unrelated to their office
any company owned by their relatives or friends
any property they buy while they are in office
answer: any transaction requiring the approval of their office
hints: Section 7(a) is not a ban on owning any business at all. It is tied to the official's own office.
The rule targets deals where officials could approve something that benefits themselves.
Read Section 7(a): the forbidden interest is in a deal that needs the approval of the official's own office. Pick the choice with that limit.

solution.methodName: Find the section, then match its exact words

steps.action: Find the rule: Section 7(a), "Financial and material interest."
Read it: officials "shall not, directly or indirectly, have any financial or material interest in any transaction requiring the approval of their office."
steps.why: A financial or material interest means you stand to gain money or property from the deal. "Indirectly" covers gaining through another person or a company.

steps.action: Note the limit: the rule is about transactions that their own office must approve.
steps.why: That is where the danger lies: the official could approve a deal that pays himself.

steps.action: The answer is: any transaction requiring the approval of their office.

trapNotes.any private business, even one unrelated: Section 7(a) is narrower. It covers only transactions "requiring the approval of their office," not every private business.
trapNotes.any company owned by their relatives or: Section 7(a) does not mention companies of relatives or friends. It covers "any transaction requiring the approval of their office."
trapNotes.any property they buy while they are in: Section 7(a) does not ban buying property while in office. It covers interests in transactions "requiring the approval of their office."
